title: DirectChange: currency converter extension for Chrome and Firefox
metaDescription: DirectChange is a free browser extension that converts every foreign price on the web into your currency, at today's live rate. Try its converter right here.
heroTitle: What is that price in your currency?
heroLede: Convert it right here, at today's live rate. This is the converter from DirectChange, a free browser extension that does it for every price on the web.
metaFree: Free, open source, no account, no tracking.
metaBrowsers: Works in Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Brave, Arc and other Chromium browsers.
demoTitle: The extension converts every price, right on the page
demoLead: A trip wishlist in six currencies, with DirectChange installed. Each price gets a small tag with its value in yours, at today's rate.
currLead: Yen, rupees, pesos or rand: the extension reads 150+ currencies and shows them in yours.
featLead: A small, free extension that does one thing: tell you what a price means to you, without leaving the page.
f1p: Rates from Coinbase for 150+ currencies, refreshed every 10 minutes. Hover any tag to see the exact rate and when it was fetched.
f2p: A “$” on a Canadian site is Canadian dollars. A “¥” on a Chinese site is yuan. DirectChange reads the domain, the page language, the shop's own data and the prices it shows.
f3p: ¥24,000, 1.234,56 €, MX$2,490, USD 45, 14 000 bahts, Rs 900… It even handles prices split across the page's HTML.
f4p: A small tag that adapts to light and dark pages. It's isolated from the site's styles, so it never breaks a layout.
f5p: Follows your browser by default, or pick a language in the settings. Right-to-left languages included.
f6p: No account, no analytics. The extension reads the page on your device and never sends it anywhere.
s1p: Add DirectChange to Chrome, Firefox, Edge or Brave. It's free and takes ten seconds.
s2p: Euro, dollar, yen, rupee… any of 150+ currencies. It defaults to your region's currency.
s3p: Foreign prices get a small badge with their value in your currency, wherever you are on the web.
convTitle: The same converter, one click away on any site
convLead: This is the extension's real popup, working. Open it on any shop: DirectChange already knows the site's currency and has your budget converted into it.
c1s: It counts the prices on the page and picks the one the site really uses, even on a .com.
c2s: 1,000 € on a Japanese site? ≈ ¥175,700, before you even type.
c3s: Swap currencies in one click. Your last amount is kept for next time.
a1: DirectChange is a free, open-source browser extension that converts prices into your own currency as you browse. It puts a small tag with the converted amount right after every foreign price on a web page, at today's live rate, and adds a quick converter to your browser toolbar.
a2: Yes. DirectChange is free, with no paid plan, no ads and no account. It's open source under the MIT License, so anyone can read the code on GitHub.
q3: Which browsers does it work in?
a3: Chrome, Edge, Brave, Arc and other Chromium browsers, through the Chrome Web Store, and Firefox on desktop and Android, through Firefox Add-ons. Safari isn't supported yet.
q4: Where do the exchange rates come from?
a4: From Coinbase's public exchange-rate API, refreshed every 10 minutes, with open.er-api.com as a daily fallback. It covers more than 150 currencies. Hover a tag to see the exact rate, when it was fetched and its source.
q5: How does it know which currency a site uses?
a5: A “$” isn't always US dollars. DirectChange reads the currency the shop declares in its product data, then the country domain (.ca, .com.au, .jp…), then the page language. Explicit symbols like € or C$ and codes like USD are never reinterpreted.
q6: Can it include my card's foreign transaction fee?
a6: Yes. Enter your card's fee abroad in the popup, for example 2%, and every tag shows what the price really costs you, fee included. The card that opens on hover shows the breakdown.
a7: No. The extension reads prices on your device and never sends page content, URLs or browsing history anywhere. Its only network requests fetch exchange rates, and they say nothing about you.
langLead: This page follows your browser's language. Pick another one here or at the top of the page.
closeText: The DirectChange extension collects nothing. The only requests it makes fetch exchange rates, and they say nothing about you or the pages you visit. The code is open source, so you can check.
madeBy: Made with care by Guillaume Gautier.
pitchText: The free extension for Chrome, Firefox, Edge and Brave puts your price next to every foreign price, on any website. No more copy-paste.
demoHint: Hover or tap a tag to see the exact rate.
